correctness.rationale: D=-pq+3p+3q+3. For p≥7 it is negative; p=3 gives D=12 and q≥13 is excluded because the divisors below 12 are {1,2,3,6}; p=5 forces q=7 and D=4, impossible from two distinct divisors. Fresh brute force below 100 reproduces only 30 and 66; the frozen verifier extends bounded regression below 1000 but is not used for exhaustiveness.

evidence: Both explicitly concern exactly two distinct prime factors.
Those theorems do not constrain a second odd prime support; positivity here forces p∈{3,5}.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The 2pq theorem is not mechanically implied.

evidence: For n=2pq, the definition is equivalent to two distinct divisors summing to D=-pq+3p+3q+3.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The prior classifications have one odd-prime support, not two.

evidence: OEIS contains 30 and 66 but states no infinite-family completeness result.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Database membership is not coverage of the classification.

originality.rationale: The 2023 and 2025 primary papers classify 2-near-perfect numbers with exactly two distinct prime factors, not the squarefree three-prime family 2pq. OEIS A341475 lists 30 and 66 but gives no exhaustion theorem for 2pq; Resultary returns the audited result as the exact hit.
residual_risks: An unindexed note or computational repository could contain the same 2pq classification.

source_inspections.evidence: Explicitly restricted to exactly two prime factors.
source_inspections.title: Complete characterization of 2-near perfect numbers with exactly 2 prime factors

value.rationale: After the exactly-two-prime-factor classification, squarefree 2pq is the simplest natural three-prime-support layer and the theorem gives a complete infinite-family classification.
residual_risks: An unindexed note or computational repository could contain the same 2pq classification.

final_claim: For odd primes p<q, the squarefree integer 2pq is 2-near-perfect exactly for 30 and 66.
scientific_limitations: An unindexed note or computational repository could contain the same 2pq classification.
Nonsquarefree three-prime-support numbers remain outside scope.
